summary: Iteration 8 — Backend coverage for Lodgify Channel Manager + Inbox integration. New file /app/backend/tests/test_lodgify_channel.py (20 tests, all green in ~12s) tests every endpoint listed in the review request against the REAL Lodgify Public API v2 using the provided key on an isolated TEST user (conftest creates fresh user_TEST_* + session_token in Mongo, no collision with production data). Verified: (1) POST /api/channel/connect returns 400 for invalid key and {ok:true, provider:'lodgify', properties_count>=1} for the real key (24 properties). (2) GET /api/channel/status returns connected=true with correct properties_count/mapped_count (0 before import, ==total after). (3) POST /api/channel/import-properties imports all Lodgify props on first call, imported=0 on second call (idempotent via lodgify_id lookup). (4) GET /api/channel/remote-properties returns list where every item has imported=true after the import. (5) POST /api/channel/sync returns {imported, updated, unmapped, conversations, total}; first sync imported>=1, second sync imported==0 and updated == (prev.imported + prev.updated). (6) GET /api/inbox returns list with guest_name/property_name/source/arrival/departure/thread_uid. (7) GET /api/inbox/{thread_uid} returns normalized messages array with id/text/date/mine (bool) and HTML stripped. (8) All /channel/* and /inbox/* endpoints return 401 without Authorization. (9) POST /api/channel/sync BEFORE importing any property returns 400 with a detail message mentioning 'logement'. (10) PUT /api/properties/{id} without lodgify_id in the body preserves the existing mapping (verified both via response and follow-up GET). Full regression run: 87/87 pytest green (was 67/67 at iteration 7). Server code untouched; no bugs found.
action_items: No blocking issues — Lodgify integration and Inbox endpoints work end-to-end against the live Lodgify Public API v2. Optional frontend self-test by main agent (behind Google OAuth): (a) Parametres → connecter Lodgify avec la clé → doit afficher 24 logements; (b) importer les logements → 24 apparaissent dans /logements; (c) synchroniser → une centaine de conversations dans l'Inbox avec badge OTA (Airbnb / Booking / Vrbo); (d) ouvrir un thread → messages voyageurs affichés avec bulles 'moi' pour Owner.
critical_code_review_comments: LodgifyAdapter._get (server.py:817-828) correctly maps 401/403 → HTTP 400 'Clé API Lodgify invalide' for the caller, and 4xx/5xx from Lodgify → HTTP 502, with 3-attempt exponential backoff on 429/5xx — good.

channel_connect (server.py:897-916) uses upsert on channel_settings keyed by user_id so re-connecting with a new key overwrites cleanly. api_key is stored plaintext in Mongo — acceptable for this stage but consider encryption-at-rest or field-level encryption before production.

channel_import_properties (server.py:959-978) uses idempotency check by {user_id, lodgify_id} — matches spec. However it does NOT update fields for existing mappings (fresh Lodgify data won't propagate on re-import). Not a bug per spec but worth flagging as a UX consideration.

channel_sync (server.py:981-1077) correctly returns {imported, updated, unmapped, conversations, total}, deduplicates by lodgify_id, maps status via LODGIFY_STATUS_MAP with canceled_at/is_deleted → 'annulee', calls ensure_cleaning() for non-cancelled bookings, and upserts conversations by (user_id, thread_uid) with $setOnInsert.unread=false.

update_property (server.py:223-236) pops lodgify_id from the update dict only when the field is None → mapping is preserved for PUTs that omit the field (verified by test_13). Confirmed this fix works as intended.

Minor: channel_sync counts 'conversations' as the total number of bookings with a thread_uid (server.py:1070) — includes duplicates because it increments even on upsert-update. Documentation may want 'threads_touched' semantics. Not blocking.

Minor: inbox_thread (server.py:1090-1118) treats m.get('type') == 'Owner' as the only 'mine' case. If Lodgify ever introduces a distinct owner-role value, the flag would silently return False. Consider a whitelist or a case-insensitive check.

Minor: inbox/{thread_uid} silently returns HTTP 200 with empty messages when the conversation doesn't belong to the user (get_thread hits Lodgify directly with the raw uid, bypassing user ownership). Consider requiring an existing conversation row for the current user before calling Lodgify.

Test suite creates channel_settings + ~24 imported properties + ~380 reservations + ~350 interventions + N conversations under that isolated user_id, then a module-scoped autouse teardown wipes channel_settings/conversations/interventions and the conftest teardown wipes properties/reservations/users/sessions. Real Lodgify data is left untouched.
